events.name: Hector Trophée I
events.description: The inaugural Hector Trophée competition was held in 2014 at Pickala Golf's Forest Course, marking the beginning of a prestigious amateur golf event that would grow in popularity and reputation over the years. While a markedly small event featuring a somewhat questionable field and a plethora of suspected rules violations, the first Hector Trophée set the stage for future tournaments, showcasing the talent and competitive spirit of amateur golfers from around the world.

events.name: Hector Trophée II
events.description: For 2015, Hector Trophée returned to the beautiful Siuntio area and Pickala Golf for a much-awaited Hector Trophée II. Starting to gain momentum as a premier amateur golf event, Hector Trophée II featured many of Finland's most promising young atheletes and Mikko Oesch. The shortness of most holes combined with the ever-present water on the Seaside course tested these talented players' adaptability and strategic skills, providing an engaging and dynamic event.

events.name: Hector Trophée III
events.description: The serene Kurk Golf in Finland set the stage for Hector Trophée III on July 21, 2016. The demanding venue for the tournament tested the golfers' resilience, versatility and strategic thinking throughout the one-day event, facing challenging course conditions at the swamp-like mud pit repurposed as a golf course.

events.name: Hector Trophée IV
events.description: On July 28, 2017, Hector Trophée returned to Pickala Golf for Hector Trophée IV. Incorporating multiple formats into a one-day competitive golf outing, Hector Trophée IV is considered by many to have been the last great event before a three-year drop in quality as some of the top players took a hiatus from participating in Hector events through 2018-2019. This format diversity highlighted the players’ tactical skills and endurance.

events.name: Hector Trophée V
events.description: At Sand Valley in Poland, the Hector Trophée V in 2018 unfolded over August 3-5, featuring a combination of stroke play, stableford, best ball, and scramble. This variety in formats heightened the competitive spirit and showcased the participants’ strategic acumen and resilience towards high levels of alcohol in their blood.

events.name: Hector Trophée VI
events.description: The Hector Trophée went abroad for a second year running in 2019, to Golf & Spa Resort Konopiště in Czechia, where Hector Trophée VI ran from September 20 to 22 across the resort's Radecký and d'Este courses. The field grew by half, from sixteen players to twenty-four in twelve pairs, making it the largest turnout the event had seen.

events.name: Hector Trophée 2020
events.description: Tahko Golf in Finland was the venue for the Hector Trophée 2020, occurring from September 10-13 despite a global pandemic and torrential rain reminiscent of an apocalypse on first two days of competition. The tournament’s format blended stroke play, stableford, best ball, and scramble, providing a comprehensive challenge that culminated in a dynamic competition.

events.name: Hector Trophée 2021
events.description: The Hector Trophée 2021, held at the Penati Golf Resort in Slovakia from September 1-4, offered a diverse competition format including stroke play, stableford, best ball, and scramble. This format tested the golfers' adaptability and skill, making for an engaging and multifaceted event.

events.name: Hector Trophée 2022
events.description: In 2022, the Quellness Golf Resort in Germany hosted the eclectic Hector Trophée, from September 14-17. This tournament featured a unique mix of stroke play, stableford, best ball, and scramble formats, showcasing the versatility and strategic depth of the world’s elite amateur golfers.

events.name: Hector Trophée 2023
events.description: The world's top amateur golfers gathered to compete in the prestigious Hector Trophée 2023. Hosted at the scenic Diamond Country Club in Austria from September 23-26, this annual event showcased a thrilling 4-day stroke play format. The elite competitors battled for the honor of claiming the esteemed Hector Trophée, adding another chapter to this celebrated tournament's history.

events.name: Hector Trophée 2024
events.description: The world's best amateur golfers will once again face off with each other in Hector Trophée 2024. The tournament will be played at La Finca and Villamartin. The tournament will be played in the classic 4-day stroke play format and the proud winners will be awarded with the prestigious Hector Trophée.

events.name: Hector Trophée 2025
events.description:
The world’s best amateur golfers are set to compete once again in Hector Trophée 2025, this time at the stunning Empordà Golf, where the Forest and Dunes courses will provide a challenging yet breathtaking backdrop for the battle. Following last year’s classic format, the tournament will span four days and six rounds of intense stroke play, culminating in the crowning of this year’s champions.

However, unlike in previous years, the players won’t be rushing to the airport after the final putt drops—fueling speculation that the 2025 edition will go down as the most legendary (and most boozy) finale in Hector Trophée history. Expect fierce competition, unforgettable moments, and a celebration worthy of the sport’s finest amateur talents.

events.name: Hector Trophée 2026
events.description:
Hector Trophee returns to Golf & Spa Resort Konopiste in 2026, where the iconic Radecky and d'Este courses will once again decide who earns the season's biggest bragging rights. Over four days of pressure-packed competition, players will take on Radecky's full championship challenge through dense forest corridors, expansive bunkering, and demanding greens that reward precise iron play and steady putting nerves.

The test only tightens on d'Este, where narrower fairways, punishing rough, and a strategy-first layout force disciplined choices from the first tee to the final putt. With momentum swinging between two very different par-72 tracks and every shot counting, Hector Trophee 2026 is set up for another classic week in Konopiste.

events.name: Hector Matchplay 2024
events.description: 16 of the world's best amateur golfers face each other in a sequence of grueling head-to-head battles to the lip-out bogey. This matchplay tournament format uses a single elimination bracket, making the stakes high from the very start.

events.name: Hector Matchplay 2025
events.description: Sixteen passionate amateur golfers go head-to-head in a series of competitive matchplay duels, where every putt counts — even the ones that just miss. The single-elimination format means there’s no room for error, as each match decides who advances and who goes home.

events.name: Hector Matchplay 2026
events.description: ~~Sixteen~~ ~~Fifteen~~ Sixteen dedicated amateur golfers battle it out in a series of intense matchplay contests, where every stroke matters — including the near misses. With a straight knockout format, there’s no second chance: each match determines who moves on and who’s eliminated.

courses.name: Adamstal - Championship
courses.description_short: The "Championship Course" of the Adamstal golf club is quite sporty: the professionals of the European Challenge Tour, who made several guest appearances, were able to find that out. Thanks to up to five tees per hole, the course is still fair for golfers of all levels. Another plus: The "Championship Course" is fully e-car compatible – even a challenge should be a pleasure.

description_long.content: In the middle of the Lower Austrian Alpine foothills lies the Adamstal Golf Club, one of the most spectacular golf courses in Europe, grandiose in design and always immaculately maintained.

Designer Jeff Howes has succeeded in skillfully integrating streams and terrain levels, forest clearings and rock formations into the impressive landscape. The varied foothills of the Alps thus naturally determine the rhythm of the fairways and green landscapes.

Therefore, it comes as no surprise that the Adamstal Golf Club has already voted Austria's Golf Course of the Year six times by a jury of experts and recently voted one of the top two most popular golf courses in Europe for the fourth time in an online survey (Golf Guide Award). Adamstal has also been one of the leading golf courses since 2002.

Club president Franz Wittmann: "There is hardly a golf course like ours in Adamstal anywhere else in the world. Not only our international guests are impressed. A round at Adamstal is certainly a unique experience that you will never forget."

courses.name: Diamond Country Club - Country
courses.description_short: The sophisticated 14-hole Country course calls for relaxed rounds throughout the week, and for a quick round during busy times while captivate players with its equally perfect condition as Diamond Country Club's championship-length European Tour course.

description_long.content: Diamond Country Club, located in Atzenbrugg, Austria, is one of the premier golfing destinations in Europe. This world-class golf resort offers a golfing experience set amidst beautiful natural surroundings, with impeccably maintained fairways, greens, and water features.

Designed by Jeremy Pern, Diamond Country Club features three courses: the championship-length 18-hole Diamond course, and its two smaller brothers, the 14-hole Country and 9-hole Park courses. Each course provides unique challenges and stunning views, making for a diverse and engaging round of golf. Each layout includes wide fairways, strategically placed bunkers, and water hazards that demand precise shot-making and thoughtful strategy.

The sophisticated 14-hole Country course calls for relaxed rounds throughout the week, and for a quick round during busy times while captivate players with its equally perfect condition as Diamond Country Club's championship-length European Tour course.

courses.name: Diamond Country Club - Diamond
courses.description_short: Nothing is as precise as the knivesof our greenkeepers, who work daily to ensure maintenance and improvement of the heart of the resort – the 18-hole European Tour Diamond Course. They meticulously remove bushes and branches on and off the Fairways to facilitate precise shots – even from tougher spots. The short mown Rough, as well as the neat Greens, enable the best Golf, always accompanied by striking water hazards surrounding the centrally located 10-hectare lake. Enjoy the impressive Diamond Course and walk in the footsteps of European Tour professionals.

description_long.content: Designed by Englishman Jeremy Pern, who fashioned the exciting Dartmouth Country Club in Devon, the Diamond has very quickly established itself as one of the best courses in Austria.

With plenty of water to focus the mind, the Diamond opened for play in 2002 and it’s a mighty challenge which stretches out to 6,810 metres from the championship tips. Choose your tee carefully and avoid your macho instinct or you’ll be masochistic with your card.

After playing the first hole – with water running down the left side of the fairway – you could be forgiven for wondering over the next five holes what all the fuss is about in relation to water hazards here. Then you will discover that eight of the remaining twelve holes feature lakes and ponds which threaten tee shots, approach shots and, at some holes, both.

The two par three holes on the back nine – the 175-metre 11th and 145-metre 15th – are played to island greens where anything wayward off the tee will sink in the drink. The 418-metre, par four, closing hole has water on the left and out of bounds on the right of the fairway, so accuracy is called for right to the very last shot on the Diamond course.

Since 2010, the Austrian Open (badged the Lyoness Open from 2012 to 2017) has been staged on the Diamond course at Diamond Country Club. Spain’s José Manuel Lara won the 2010 event and saved his European Tour card in the process after beating David Lynn in a play-off.

Fast-forward to 2018 and Diamond Country Club will be remembered for genuine innovation. The Shot Clock Masters made history as the first tournament in professional golf to use a shot clock on every stroke as part of the European Tour’s bid to combat slow play. All players were timed on every shot, and on each occasion a player failed to hit his shot within the time limits, a one-shot penalty was added to his score for that hole. Interestingly, not one single professional ranked in the world top one hundred played in the 2018 event (which Finland’s Mikko Korhonen won) and only four players were penalised over the four days where round times were recorded as being significantly quicker than the season average.

courses.name: Diamond Country Club - Park
courses.description_short: The family-friendly 9-hole Park course - our public course - is the ideal place not only for beginners but also for the occasional after-work round.

description_long.content: Diamond Country Club, located in Atzenbrugg, Austria, is one of the premier golfing destinations in Europe. This world-class golf resort offers a golfing experience set amidst beautiful natural surroundings, with impeccably maintained fairways, greens, and water features.

Designed by Jeremy Pern, Diamond Country Club features three courses: the championship-length 18-hole Diamond course, and its two smaller brothers, the 14-hole Country and 9-hole Park courses. Each course provides unique challenges and stunning views, making for a diverse and engaging round of golf. Each layout includes wide fairways, strategically placed bunkers, and water hazards that demand precise shot-making and thoughtful strategy.
The family-friendly 9-hole Diamond Park Course - our Public Course - is the ideal place not only for beginners but also for the occasional after-work round.

courses.name: Empordà Dunes

contact.address: Ctra. de Palafrugell a Torroella de Montgrí, 17257 Gualta, Girona, Spain

courses.description_short: Empordà Dunes is a bold and wind-swept challenge. Where others saw unremarkable marshland, architect Robert von Hagge saw an opportunity to craft a course of pure imagination. Empordà Dunes is a masterful blend of rolling inland dunes, unpredictable coastal winds, and modern water hazards, capturing the soul of traditional Scottish links while adding its own unique character.

Stretching 6300 meters, this dynamic course rewards players who combine precision, strategy, and creativity. The ever-changing wind conditions make club selection a constant challenge, while the open layout demands a keen eye for positioning. With its thrilling mix of natural beauty and strategic design, Empordà Dunes delivers an exhilarating test for golfers of all levels.

Empordà Golf's two world-class courses, designed by Robert von Hagge and Rick Baril, offer a unique experience in every round. This European Tour hosting resort combines the joy of playing golf with the pleasure of walking surrounded by nature.

contact.address: Ctra. de Palafrugell a Torroella de Montgrí, 17257 Gualta, Girona, Spain

Nestled in the heart of a century-old pine forest, Empordà Forest offers a truly immersive golfing experience, where nature and design blend seamlessly. Protected from coastal winds by towering pines, this hidden gem of the Costa Brava presents a course that is as strategic as it is scenic.

courses.name: Konopiště - d'Este
courses.description_short: The d'Este course at Konopiště is a par-72 championship course that stretches up to 6,086 meters from the back tee. Located in the beautiful Czech countryside at the Konopiště golf resort, the D’ Este course is tougher than its sibling, Radecký, and requires skill and golf planning. The key is to stay on the fairways and off the rough – as several golfers have found that it can be quite treacherous.

description_long.content: Konopiště Golf Resort in Benešov, Czech Republic is an unparalleled experience. Not only is it a short distance from Prague, but it also offers two par 72 championship courses and a nine-hole academy course, making it the perfect choice for a golf trip. As couples, groups or for training stays.

The 4-star Manor Hotel at Konopiště Resort offers comfortable accommodation in the beautiful surroundings of the beautifully converted manor house. With roots dating back to the 14th century, this hotel has been beautifully remodeled and now has the facilities and amenities required of a good modern hotel, including satellite TV, safe, minibar, private bathroom and more.

The d'Este course at Konopiště is a par-72 championship course that stretches up to 6,086 meters from the back tee. The D’ Este course is tougher than its sibling, Radecký, and requires skill and golf planning. The key is to stay on the fairways and off the rough – as several golfers have found that it can be quite treacherous. While shorter than its bigger brother, D’Este is indeed not without its challenges; the fairways are narrowed in places by the property’s impressive forest, so it’s often wise to play conservatively to achieve a good position.

Simply walking in this magnificent setting is an experience in itself as the d’Este course is immersed in the surrounding nature, with several of its fairways lined by the park’s ancient oaks. The course’s highlight and certainly the most picturesque hole is the 9th, which features an island green accessible only by a narrow walkway.

courses.name: Konopiště - Radecký
courses.description_short: The Radecký course at Konopiště is an impressive course cut through a beautiful forest area. This championship course is up to 6,484 meters from the back tee. Named after the property’s original residents, Radecký was built in consultation with the European PGA and is a great test even for the low handicapper.
